cases.sentence: А потом я пошел в центр, потому что это у меня всегда так: когда я ищу Кремль, я неизменно попадаю на ___.
cases.explain: «Курский вокзал» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Then I headed for the center of town, since it always works out that when I’m looking for the Kremlin I end up at the Kursk Station. In fact, I really did have to go to the Kursk Station and not the center of town, but I set out for the center all the same in order to see the Kremlin at least once, meanwhile thinking, "‘I won’t see any Kremlin anyway and I'll end up mght at the Kursk Station."’

cases.sentence: Не потому, конечно, обидно, что к ___ я так вчера и не вышел.
cases.explain: «Курскому вокзалу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Now I'm almost in tears feeling sorry for myself. Not because I didn’t get to the Kursk Station yesterday, of course.

cases.sentence: Все знают – все, кто в беспамятстве попадал в подъезд, а на рассвете выходил из него, – все знают, какую тяжесть в сердце пронес я по этим сорока ступеням ___ и какую тяжесть вынес на воздух.
cases.explain: «чужого подъезда» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: I came outside when it was already getting light. Everyone knows—everyone who has ended up out cold in a hallway and left at dawn—everyone knows what a heavy heart I carried down those forty steps in a strange hallway, and what a weight I carried outside.

cases.sentence: А вон – этот пидор в ___ скребет тротуар.
cases.explain: «коричневой куртке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: "It’s nothing," I said to myself. "Nothing. There’s a pharmacy, see? And over there, that creep in the brown jacket scraping the sidewalk. You see that too? So calm down. Everything is going along as it should. If you want to turn left, Venichka, turn left, I’m not forcing you to do anything. If you want to turn right, turn right."’

cases.sentence: О, эта ___ в сердце! о, иллюзорность бедствия! о, непоправимость!
cases.explain: «утренняя ноша» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: I turned right, staggering a bit from the cold and from grief, yes, from the cold and from grief. Oh, that morning burden in the heart! Oh, the illusory nature of calamity. Oh, the irretrievable! What’s worse about this burden which no one has yet called by any name, what’s worse—paralysis, or nausea? Nervous exhaustion, or mortal sorrow somewhere in the region of the heart? But, if that’s all equal, then all the same what’s worse about it—stupefaction, or fever?

cases.sentence: Если даже ты пойдешь налево – попадешь на ___; если прямо – все равно на Курский вокзал.
cases.explain: «Курский вокзал» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: ‘It’s OK, it’s OK,"’ I said to myself. "Back to the wind and get going slowly. And breathe slow, slow. Breathe so that your knees don’t get tangled. Go on, anywhere. It’s all the same where. Even if you turn left, you'll end up at the Kursk Station; or straight, all the same, the Kursk Station. Therefore, turn right, so that you'll get there for sure. Oh, vanity.

cases.sentence: Сколько ___ оно вплело во всех нас, в бездомных и тоскующих шатенов!
cases.explain: «лишних седин» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: ‘Oh, the ephemeral! Oh, that most helpless and shameful of times in the life of my people, the time from dawn until the liquor stores open up! How many unneces- sary gray hairs has it caused us homeless and grieving brunets! Let’s go, Venichka, let’s go."’
